question: What defines an idiosyncratic drug reaction compared to a normal drug side effect?

options.A: It is a predictable result of the main drug action
options.B: It affects every patient who takes the medication
options.C: It happens only when the drug dose is doubled
options.D: It occurs unexpectedly at standard doses

explanation: Idiosyncratic reactions happen unpredictably in a few individuals taking normal, standard doses of a medicine. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why are true idiosyncratic reactions not classified as regular dose-dependent side effects?

options.A: They can be easily calculated using the patient's body weight
options.B: They do not relate to the drug's primary pharmacological action
options.C: They disappear immediately after the first dose is stopped
options.D: They only show up when the patient takes an overdose

explanation: These reactions stem from unique patient factors rather than the drug's intended action, meaning changing the dose does not prevent them. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which system in the body is mainly responsible for variations in how drugs are broken down?
explanation: Genetic differences in cytochrome P450 enzymes heavily influence how drugs are metabolized or turned into active compounds. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h2)

question: How can genetic differences in liver enzymes lead to an unexpected drug reaction?

options.A: By doubling the speed of normal therapeutic blood levels
options.B: By stopping the stomach from absorbing the medication entirely
options.C: By making the drug pass through the kidneys too quickly
options.D: By creating toxic byproducts through alternative breakdown pathways

explanation: When normal pathways fail, alternative routes can generate unstable chemical byproducts that damage cells. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is a hapten in drug-related immune reactions?

options.A: A small drug molecule that binds to body proteins to trigger an immune response
options.B: A specialized liver enzyme that breaks down toxic metabolites
options.C: A genetic marker found in patients with high drug tolerance
options.D: A protective blood cell that fights off drug toxicity

explanation: Small drug molecules act as haptens by attaching to larger body proteins, which tricks the immune system into attacking them. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h3)

question: Why do some immune drug reactions take weeks to show up after starting a medication?

options.A: Time is required for the immune system to recognize the drug-protein mix
options.B: White blood cells hide in the kidneys until the dose is doubled
options.C: The drug takes at least thirty days to reach the liver
options.D: The body must completely exhaust its normal enzyme supply first

explanation: Immune-mediated reactions often take time because the body needs to build a primary immune response against the combined drug-protein structure. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h3)

question: Which two organ systems are most commonly targeted by severe idiosyncratic drug reactions?
explanation: The liver and the skin are the most frequent sites for severe, life-threatening idiosyncratic drug reactions. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h4)

question: A patient on a new medication has yellow eyes, dark urine, and discomfort on the upper right side of the abdomen. What is the likely cause?
explanation: Jaundice and upper right abdominal pain point directly to liver involvement, a key sign of severe idiosyncratic drug reactions. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why must nurses always ask patients about herbal supplements during drug histories?

options.A: Herbs prevent the liver from producing any bile at all
options.B: Herbal products can also trigger unexpected adverse reactions
options.C: Traditional remedies are regulated by strict federal drug laws
options.D: Supplements always cancel out prescribed hospital medicines

explanation: Patients often forget herbs and supplements, yet these substances frequently cause unpredictable liver and immune reactions. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why is finding out exactly when symptoms started after taking a drug important for the nurse?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from ordering unnecessary blood tests
options.B: It proves whether the patient took the exact prescribed dose
options.C: It guarantees the insurance company will cover the hospital stay
options.D: It helps link the unexpected reaction to a specific drug

explanation: A clear timeline is essential because idiosyncratic reactions do not follow regular dose rules, making timing the best clue to the cause. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the most important first step when an unexpected drug reaction is suspected?

options.A: Wait for laboratory confirmation before taking action
options.B: Administer a stat dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Double the IV fluid rate to flush the kidneys
options.D: Stop giving the suspected medication right away

explanation: Stopping the offending drug immediately is the single most important action to prevent further harm to tissues. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why is supportive care the main treatment for most unpredictable drug reactions?

options.A: Supportive care prevents the liver from metabolizing other drugs
options.B: The body always clears the drug within two hours naturally
options.C: Specific antidotes are rarely available for these reactions
options.D: Hospital pharmacies refuse to stock medications for rare events

explanation: Because these reactions are unusual and varied, treatment focuses on supporting failing body organs while natural recovery happens. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which agency in Nigeria is primarily responsible for receiving reports on adverse drug reactions?
explanation: NAFDAC handles pharmacovigilance and tracks adverse drug reactions nationwide in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why is detailed charting of an unusual drug reaction in a patient's record so vital?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never need any medication again
options.B: It prevents future healthcare providers from giving the dangerous drug again
options.C: It allows the hospital to bill the pharmaceutical company for damages
options.D: It proves the nurse followed every hospital protocol correctly

explanation: Clear charting ensures that everyone on the healthcare team knows the patient is dangerously sensitive to that specific drug. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h7)
